velholdt.explanation: "Velholdt" means "well-kept". It is built from "vel" (well) and "holdt" (kept). To describe a house in good condition: "Huset er meget velholdt" (The house is very well-kept). For a business that is managed well, use "veldrevet" (well-run): "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop).

velkendt.explanation: "Velkendt" means "well-known". It is built from "vel" (well) and "kendt" (known). When you know a face or a tune well yourself, it means "familiar": "et velkendt ansigt" (a familiar face).

velklædt.explanation: "Velklædt" means "well-dressed". It is built from "vel" (well) and "klædt" (dressed), from "at klæde" (to dress). To say how someone looks: "Hun ser velklædt ud" (She looks well-dressed).

velkommen.explanation: "Velkommen" means "welcome". To welcome someone to a place, add "til" (to) before the place: "Velkommen til Danmark" (Welcome to Denmark). To answer "tak" (thanks), say "selv tak" (you're welcome): "Tak for hjælpen." "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. You're welcome.)

vellykket.explanation: "Vellykket" means "successful". It is built from "vel" (well) and "lykket", from "at lykkes" (to succeed). To say an event or a trip turned out well: "Rejsen var vellykket" (The trip was successful). For a person or a company, use "succesfuld" (successful): "en succesfuld forretningsmand" (a successful businessman).

velopdragen.explanation: "Velopdragen" means "well-behaved". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at opdrage" (to bring up). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et velopdraget barn" (a well-behaved child).

velsmagende.explanation: "Velsmagende" means "tasty". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at smage" (to taste). To praise food: "Maden er velsmagende" (The food is tasty).

vemodig.explanation: "Vemodig" means "wistful". It comes from "vemod" (a soft, quiet sadness). To say how someone smiled, add "t": "Hun smilede vemodigt" (She smiled wistfully).

venlig.explanation: "Venlig" means "kind". It comes from "en ven" (a friend). To end a letter or an email: "Venlig hilsen" (Kind regards).

venlighed.explanation: "Venlighed" means "kindness". It comes from "venlig" (kind). To thank someone for being kind: "Tak for din venlighed" (Thank you for your kindness).

venligst.explanation: "Venligst" means "please". It sounds formal. To politely ask someone to wait: "Vent venligst" (Please wait).

venstre.explanation: "Venstre" means "left", as in the opposite of right. To give directions: "Drej til venstre" (Turn left). "Venstre" is also the name of a Danish political party: "Han stemmer på Venstre" (He votes for Venstre).

vent lidt.explanation: "Vent lidt" means "wait a bit". It is "vent" (the command form of "at vente", to wait) and "lidt" (a bit). To make it more polite, add "tak" (thanks): "Vent lidt, tak" (Wait a bit, please).

vest.explanation: "Vest" means "west". To say where the wind comes from: "Vinden kommer fra vest" (The wind comes from the west). It is also part of "Vestjylland" (West Jutland), the western part of Jutland, the Danish mainland.

vestlig.explanation: "Vestlig" means "westerly". It is built from "vest" (west). To say a place is in the western part of a country, use "det vestlige" (the western part): "Esbjerg ligger i det vestlige Danmark" (Esbjerg is in western Denmark).

vestpå.explanation: "Vestpå" means "west", for moving toward the west. To say a plane changes direction: "Flyet drejer vestpå" (The plane turns west). To say where a place lies, use "vest for" (west of): "Esbjerg ligger vest for Odense" (Esbjerg is west of Odense).

vi.explanation: "Vi" means "we". To say what we do: "Vi bor her" (We live here). When you mean "us", use "os" instead: "Han ser os" (He sees us).

vi ses.explanation: "Vi ses" means "see you". Literally, it is "we see each other". When you say goodbye to someone you will meet again, add the time: "Vi ses på fredag" (See you on Friday).

vi snakkes.explanation: "Vi snakkes" means "talk to you later". To end a call when you expect to speak again: "Tak for hjælpen, vi snakkes!" (Thanks for the help, talk to you later!)

vi tales ved.explanation: "Vi tales ved" means "talk soon". To end a call when you will speak again: "Jeg ringer i morgen, vi tales ved!" (I will call tomorrow, talk soon!) When you expect to meet in person, say "vi ses" (see you): "Vi ses på kontoret" (See you at the office).

via.explanation: "Via" means "via". To say the route of a trip: "Vi kører via Odense" (We drive via Odense). To say how you contact someone: "Skriv til mig via mail" (Write to me via email).

viden.explanation: "Viden" means "knowledge". It comes from "at vide" (to know). To talk about knowledge in general, use it without an article: "Viden er magt" (Knowledge is power).

videnskabelig.explanation: "Videnskabelig" means "scientific". It is built from "en videnskab" (a science), which comes from "viden" (knowledge). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et videnskabeligt forsøg" (a scientific experiment).

vidtrækkende.explanation: "Vidtrækkende" means "far-reaching". To say a change will affect many things: "Det får vidtrækkende konsekvenser" (It will have far-reaching consequences).

vidunderlig.explanation: "Vidunderlig" means "wonderful". It is built on "et vidunder" (a wonder). When you talk about an event, add "t": "Det var vidunderligt!" (That was wonderful!)
